reason: E1 and E2 show sacrificial oxidation of non-noble metals forming oxide shells that inhibit Pd diffusion and structural change, but this occurs under NO (a reactive gas) on CeO2 support, not under mild O2 on SiO2. E3 provides synthesis and catalytic data but no evidence on oxidation-induced stability. The cited evidence thus partially supports the oxidation and barrier premises but does not directly support the specific mild O2 atmosphere, SiO2 support, or high-temperature stability claims.
premises: Less noble metals (Co, Cu, Ni) in HEA nanoparticles can be selectively oxidized under mild oxidative conditions.
Selective oxidation forms oxide patches or shells on the nanoparticle surface.
These oxide patches act as physical barriers that inhibit surface atomic diffusion and sintering.
Noble metal sites (Pt, Pd) remain largely unoxidized and catalytically active under these conditions.
This mechanism preserves homogeneous single-phase structure and catalytic activity at high temperatures.
